incident_summary: On 2025-12-01 at 07:33:35 UTC, NetWitness generated six high-severity alerts for host KELLYWANG associated with user KELLYWANG\Kelly Wang. The alerts repeatedly identified a process named splunkd.exe running from C:\Users\Public\ and issuing a command line of splunkd.exe -server http://192.168.10.202:8888 -group red. The activity originated from source IP 192.168.10.204 and connected to destination IP 192.168.10.202 on port 8888, with the domain acmecorp-reset.com appearing in the alert metadata. The first alert fired at 07:33:35.204 UTC, followed by additional alerts at 07:33:35.299 UTC, 07:33:36.260 UTC, 07:33:36.262 UTC, and two more at 07:33:36.268 UTC, showing repeated outbound C2-style connections over a very short interval. Threat intelligence later associated multiple file hashes from the case with malicious detections in VirusTotal and an AlienVault OTX pulse, reinforcing that the observed host behavior was suspicious and consistent with command-and-control activity. No process lineage, privilege escalation chain, or exfiltration telemetry was provided in the case material, so the incident is limited to the observed suspicious execution and repeated network connections.
actions_taken: Reviewed all six NetWitness sub-alerts for the current case.
Correlated the alerts to the same host KELLYWANG, user KELLYWANG\Kelly Wang, source IP 192.168.10.204, and destination IP 192.168.10.202:8888.
Validated the suspicious command line referencing http://192.168.10.202:8888 and group red.
Checked threat-intelligence results for the provided hashes and confirmed malicious reputation indicators.
Assessed the case against the privilege escalation playbook and documented unsupported steps as not met.
recommended_containment: Immediately isolate host KELLYWANG (192.168.10.204) from the network using EDR or network quarantine to stop any ongoing outbound C2 sessions.
Block outbound and inbound communication to 192.168.10.202 TCP/8888 at the proxy, firewall, and EDR network controls, and add acmecorp-reset.com to a temporary deny list pending validation.
Acquire a volatile memory capture and a full disk image from KELLYWANG before remediation to preserve evidence of the splunkd.exe execution and any spawned child processes.
Collect the full process tree, command-line history, and file creation timeline for C:\Users\Public\splunkd.exe, including any copies, downloads, or alternate launchers.
Hunt enterprise-wide for the provided malicious file hashes and any execution from C:\Users\Public\, and alert on any host beaconing to 192.168.10.202:8888.
Reset or disable the credentials for KELLYWANG\Kelly Wang if the endpoint review confirms malicious execution or unauthorized use, and review recent logons for abuse.
Preserve NetWitness packet captures, proxy logs, DNS telemetry, and EDR network events for all connections tied to the six alert timestamps for analyst review.
severity_justification: High severity is appropriate because the case shows strongly suspected malicious outbound activity on an important user endpoint, repeated C2-style connections over multiple alerts, a suspicious executable launched from C:\Users\Public\, and threat-intelligence corroboration from VirusTotal and AlienVault OTX. The evidence supports a likely compromise but does not show confirmed ransomware, large-scale outage, or sensitive data exposure, so Critical is not justified.
confidence_justification: Confidence is High because multiple independent sources align: repeated NetWitness alerts, consistent user/host/IP attribution, a suspicious command line to 192.168.10.202:8888, and threat-intelligence matches for provided hashes. The main limitation is the absence of process lineage and direct endpoint execution telemetry, but the overall evidence is sufficient and internally consistent.
